summary: Zee Business lists the top 10 run-scorers and wicket-takers of the ICC Men's ODI World Cup 2023, with short profiles of each player. Virat Kohli leads the batting with 765 runs, while Mohammed Shami leads the bowling. The piece also recaps the semi-finals and the final, won by Australia over India. Some figures in the profiles differ from the tables.
one_line: Zee Business ranks the top 10 batsmen and bowlers of the 2023 ODI World Cup, led by Virat Kohli's 765 runs and Mohammed Shami's wickets.
key_facts: Australia beat India by six wickets in the ICC Men's ODI World Cup 2023 final at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad.
India beat New Zealand by 70 runs in the first semi-final on November 15 at Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai.
Australia beat South Africa by three wickets in the second semi-final on November 16 at Eden Gardens in Kolkata.
Virat Kohli tops the batting list with 765 runs in 11 matches, with three centuries, five fifties and a highest score of 117.
Rohit Sharma is second with 597 runs in 11 matches, and Quinton de Kock third with 594 runs in 10 matches.
Quinton de Kock has the most centuries in the tournament, with four.
Rachin Ravindra, a 23-year-old New Zealand all-rounder, scored 578 runs in 10 matches with three centuries and two fifties.
Mohammed Shami tops the bowling list; the table shows 23 wickets in 7 matches, while the profile says 24 wickets in six matches, conceding 257 runs.
Shami took three five-wicket hauls, including seven wickets against New Zealand in the semi-final at Wankhede Stadium.
Adam Zampa took 23 wickets, including three four-wicket hauls, conceding 515 runs, making him Australia's top wicket-taker.
Dilshan Madushanka of Sri Lanka took 21 wickets, conceding 525 runs.
Jasprit Bumrah took 20 wickets and has the best economy rate of the tournament at 4.06.
Marco Jansen, 6 feet 7 inches tall, took 17 wickets in nine matches for South Africa.
Head Coach Rahul Dravid called Shreyas Iyer the backbone of the Indian middle order.
